key_insight: Solution-phase ligand exchange enables thicker AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers, supporting demonstrated 24.0%-efficient four-terminal tandems with perovskite sub-cells.
engineering_relevance: One-step deposition of passivated AgBiS2 nanocrystals offers a route toward scalable, stable near-infrared sub-cells for thin-film tandem photovoltaics.
method: Model tandem performance using the experimental AgBiS2 absorption spectrum.
Apply solution-phase ligand exchange to preserve charge extraction in thicker nanocrystal films.
Integrate AgBiS2 with visible-absorbing perovskites in four-terminal and monolithic tandems.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 24.0% four-terminal tandem efficiency, voltage addition in monolithic tandems, and >90% efficiency retention after three months of unencapsulated dry-air storage; triple-junction efficiencies above 47.9% are modeled, not demonstrated.
watch_item: Dry-air storage stability does not establish operational durability under illumination, heat, or humidity.
paper_title: Stable AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
